body:
# Independent audit: actual applicability of the nonregular same separator

Audited source: `candidate 9158d8d941246660`, Sections 1–7.

Result: PASS for the explicitly stated continuous normal-dependent convex-field cone, simultaneous concave parameter directions, finite cap-normal controls, and both log-epsilon directions. No additional regularity of the other-fiber cap traces is required. This is not a proof of a numerical depth bound or a separator for arbitrary formal signed velocity arrays.

## 1. Dependency boundary

The compact positive minimal-bad-base framework, logarithmic-scale attainment, strictly positive finite-PL representative, geometric vanishing of the buffers, own-source interiority, and own-properness are prior inputs. Their uses here do not require the response separator that the present source constructs. In particular, Sections 1–3 of the total-force source provide geometric properness; the later entropy argument for total force is not used to obtain it. The quantitative value gap and scalar-scale attainment likewise precede the same-separator construction.

I independently checked the new bridges against the exact source balance, signed complete-cut, all-status inverse, and multicontact dependencies. The result does not replace these inputs by a generic smoothness assertion.

## 2. Full prescribed supergradient and contact finiteness

Write `F=E^(1/d)` and `f=M^(-1/N)L^(1/N)F^(d/N)`, `N=d+1`. At an own-interior mark, F has a unique continuous gradient. Since L is a finite minimum of full affine planes, its fiber superdifferential is exactly the convex hull of their active continuous gradients. Thus every selected fiber supergradient of f has the displayed form (2), and the SAME convex combination of active full plane gradients extends its L part. The established finite-hull energy supergradient extends the F part. Applying the increasing geometric mean to the two upper tangents gives the full upper tangent, not merely a local derivative identity.

Strict own concavity is also valid at PL creases: along two different interior points the F inequality is strict; strict increase in F and concavity of the geometric mean preserve that strict inequality. A fiber zero of `psi=P-h-epsilon f` is unique because psi is nonnegative convex and has an interior zero. A second interior zero contradicts strict concavity. A second boundary zero would make the segment between them zero, producing two interior zeros and the same contradiction. Hence the actual contact set used in the continuation is finite, with exactly one mark at every assigned integer base.

The right-quantile source balance is not a differentiability argument for cap mass. Local tilt clamping preserves all near-active traces on the own fiber; their proper own section makes the local tail inverse strict. The compact active slope set and the concave source maximum give the finite balance by the convex superdifferential rule and Caratheodory. The selected caps are still genuine global caps, so the full tangent inequality propagates their cover to the minimal deepest-base face. A midpoint of same-parity witnesses belongs to the deepest region by concavity, and its minimal face contains both previous minimal faces. This verifies the maximal-face parity count.

## 3. Signed physical realization

For each sampled base z, the proposed body is the intersection of `u.x+t Phi(u,z,x)<=h_z(u)`. A jointly continuous, globally finite convex field has a uniform lower linear bound on the compact normal/base sets. Taking `u=x/|x|` bounds every new fiber for small t. On the resulting common ball, the field is bounded, so support comparison and an old inball homothety give Hausdorff and radial displacement O(t), positivity, and a common radial domination bound.

The compatibility calculation (7) is exact, including negative field values: convexity gives the field inequality and the old anchored inclusion gives the support inequality. Therefore the canonical hull has precisely the constructed sampled fibers. No independent motion of a contact-constrained fiber is assumed.

At an old regular boundary point, an old active normal gives one radial derivative bound. A new active normal has old slack tending to zero; uniqueness of the old normal gives its limit and the reverse bound. This proves speed `Phi(n,z,x)` for either inward or outward motion. Nonsmooth points form a surface-null set. Finite nonnegative field sums realize the sum of speeds, and both signs of every normal-dependent affine field are legal. Supporting cap losses themselves are not asserted to add.

The parameter cone is simultaneously feasible on the same bodies: if `h+cL` is concave, then `L+t h=(1-ct)L+t(h+cL)` is concave for small positive t. Positivity holds on a fixed neighborhood. Finitely many such directions can be summed and realized on one common time interval. Both signs of affine h, both signs of L, and negative finite convex maxima are included.

## 4. Normalization and finite-contact continuation

With signed inward speed v, `M'=-D`, the logarithmic normalization has derivative `H-s_L`, because its old average is zero. Consequently

`dot f/f=(h/L-H+s_L-C_E/E+D/M)/N`.

For the old unit covariance-normalized normals,

`dot Gamma_j=D/(2M)-J_j/(2M)+grad Gamma_j.u'_j`.

Differentiating the full exact contact minimum, including epsilon(t)=epsilon exp(st), gives exactly (12): the D coefficient is `-(N+2)/(2NM)`; the logarithmic boundary coefficient is `-s_L/N`; the parameter coefficients are `-h/(N L)+H/N`; and the scale coefficient is `-s`. The cap-plane coefficient is the weighted `nu_j.Y` minus the buffer's weighted norm variation. No derivative of a PL gradient, contact optimizer, or optimized parameter is introduced.

Compact contact localization and the uniform signed energy envelope justify taking the minimum of these finitely many linear contact coefficients. The old interior marks remain admissible for small t. Remote old boundary points have strictly positive contact deficit, and uniform continuity excludes new remote minimizing contacts. The exact common-quantile equation therefore gives an actual cover of all assigned sampled fibers. All other bases retain their strict gap by joint upper semicontinuity and the finite base set.

## 5. Conservative loss, compact dual, and invariances

For every selected cap the own proper coarea is strictly positive. Dropping only the nonnegative inside hinge keeps the full inside-fiber body loss and produces (14), a concave loss increasing onto the real line in its threshold velocity. The outside hinge is represented by densities in [0,1] on the actual old supporting facets; the same density enters the body, coarea, and full moment terms. Its weak-star moment image is compact, and all equalization denominators have a positive proper-coarea lower bound.

For finite tests, the response hypograph is convex and disjoint from the open positive orthant by actual minimality. Closedness of the image cone is unnecessary for that separation. The contact minimum is another finite infimum of linear branch losses. The resulting weights can be represented by finite cap/contact weights and weighted facet selectors `0<=zeta_j<=omega_j`. Their coarea equations bound all contact weights. Thus the full dual variable set is weak-star compact. Every additional integrable test imposes a closed inequality. The finite-intersection argument gives one common dual for the entire explicit cone, not separate duals for separate tests.

Both signs of the free log-scale variable force `Delta=M tau`, since the normalized conservative improvement is `ell-beta D+M tau s`. Shared cap-normal variables yield the shared contact barycenter, not one individual centroid equation per source. Both signs of normal-dependent affine physical fields give the stated localized affine equalities. The parameter tests produce the SAME-e volume certificate.

Finally, exact fiber-affine composition supplies affine null directions without inserting the discontinuous formal PL jet `-grad L.V` into the continuous parameter cone. This removes the potential crease circularity: source-gradient uniqueness is a later consequence of the volume contact theorem, not an assumption used here.

## 6. Scope retained

The proof discharges the earlier conditional continuation and physical-cone premises at the selected sufficiently small logarithmic-scale minima, under the established positive compact minimal-bad framework. It leaves intact all later limits: inverse-parameter boundary concentration is possible; the volume martingale is tilted; original row means need not be their source marks; and no sharp mixed depth payment follows from the separator alone.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
